title: Japanese course from hiragana to JLPT N1 · Glossa
description: A free Japanese course from hiragana to advanced: 80 modules that follow the grammar of JLPT N5 to N1 and teach about 1,000 kanji, with feedback that explains.

card.title: Japanese
card.text: From hiragana and katakana to advanced Japanese, with about 1,000 kanji and the grammar of JLPT N5 to N1.

heading: Learn Japanese with the grammar explained.
lead: A complete Japanese course for English speakers, from your first hiragana to advanced Japanese: 80 modules in eight tiers that follow the grammar of JLPT N5 to N1. About 1,000 kanji are taught step by step, particles, verb forms and keigo are explained directly, and every exercise tells you why an answer is right or wrong.
fineprint: The whole course is free. Specialization courses, JLPT practice papers, conversation practice and the other extras are part of Premium, €8.99 a month or €69.99 a year.

panel.label: The course, tier by tier

items.title: Scripts and sounds
items.text: Hiragana, katakana, typing kana, pitch, the first sentences with です.

items.title: First kanji and everyday basics
items.text: First kanji and numbers, polite verbs, both kinds of adjective.

items.title: Daily life
items.text: The te-form, requests and permission, counters, comparison.

items.title: Plain forms
items.text: は and が, plain forms and casual speech, giving and receiving.

items.title: Building fluency
items.text: Noun-modifying clauses, conditionals, the passive, the first keigo.

items.title: Intermediate
items.text: The causative, transitive and intransitive pairs, the written style.

items.title: Upper intermediate
items.text: Business keigo, N2 grammar, kanji compounds, the news.

items.title: Advanced
items.text: Classical forms, N1 expressions, register, spoken and regional Japanese.

panel.note: 80 modules. The tiers follow JLPT N5 to N1. The last tiers also cover topics such as politics, the economy, science, history, literature and law.

sections.heading: What the course teaches, and how

items.title: The scripts first
items.text: The first tier teaches hiragana, katakana and typing kana, the rhythm and pitch of Japanese, and the first sentences, before the kanji begin.

items.title: About 1,000 kanji, step by step
items.text: Kanji are taught from the second tier on, with furigana you can hide when you want to read without them.

items.title: The grammar taught directly
items.text: Particles such as は and が, the te-form, plain forms, conditionals, the passive and causative, and keigo each have their own modules, explained in plain English with examples.

items.title: Feedback that says why
items.text: Every answer gets feedback with a reason and a link to the grammar rule behind it. Every Japanese word can be tapped for its reading, meaning, forms and audio.

items.title: Pronunciation feedback
items.text: Speaking exercises assess your pronunciation of Japanese sentences word by word.

items.title: A placement test
items.text: If you already know some Japanese, the placement test shows where to start, so you do not have to work through what you know.

sections.heading: Practice papers for the JLPT
sections.intro: The course has timed practice papers for the Japanese-Language Proficiency Test (日本語能力試験), two papers at each of its five levels. Like the real test, they cover language knowledge, reading and listening; the JLPT has no writing or speaking test. What the papers cover and how they differ from the real test.

sections.heading: Japanese for your field
sections.intro: Thirteen specialization courses, nine modules each, in three stages: Foundations after Tier 3, Working vocabulary after Tier 5 and Professional after Tier 7. Each teaches the vocabulary and register of one field.

items.question: Do I need to know hiragana before I start?
items.answer: No. The first tier starts with hiragana, then katakana and typing kana on a phone or computer, before any kanji.

items.question: How many kanji does the course teach?
items.answer: About 1,000, step by step from the second tier on, with furigana you can hide. The JLPT's earlier specifications expected about 2,000 kanji at the level N1 replaced, so learning the rest, mostly for reading, is part of preparing for N1.

items.question: Does the course prepare me for the JLPT?
items.answer: The tiers follow the grammar of N5 to N1, and Premium has two timed practice papers at each level. The papers show the share of points you got, not a JLPT score, and no course can promise a pass.

items.question: Is the Japanese course really free?
items.answer: Yes. All 80 modules, the grammar reference, word practice, the placement test and 5 Ask AI questions a day are free. The JLPT papers, specializations, stories, conversation practice and the other extras are part of Premium.

items.question: Can I practise speaking?
items.answer: The course's speaking exercises give feedback on your pronunciation word by word. With Premium you can also hold typed or spoken conversations with an AI character in 38 situations, and practise pronunciation on sentences you type.

closing.heading: Start with hiragana, or wherever you are.
closing.text: Sign in with Google, take the placement test if you already know some Japanese, and open the first module.
